$comment: Venue profiles used by pubstyle.py, plot scripts, check_figure.py, lint_paper.py, check_env.py and layout_check.py (--venue). Widths in inches. page_limit = main-body pages for a regular submission (null when it varies by year or track: pass --page-limit). Always confirm limits and required sections against the current call for papers.

ieee.name: IEEE conferences and Transactions (IEEEtran)
ieee.notes: Page limits differ per venue (e.g. IEEE S&P counts the body separately from references and appendices). Limitations usually close the Discussion.

acm.name: ACM conferences (acmart, sigconf)
acm.notes: No fixed caption-case convention; keep one style throughout. Page limits are set per conference (e.g. CCS).

acl.name: ACL / EMNLP / NAACL (*ACL style files)
acl.notes: Long papers: 8 pages of content (short papers: 4); references, the Limitations section and an ethics statement do not count. Pass --page-limit 4 for short papers. The style files come from the ACL style-file repository, not TeX Live: copy them next to main.tex.

neurips.name: NeurIPS (neurips_*.sty)
neurips.notes: 9 content pages at submission; references, appendix and the paper checklist do not count. The style file name changes every year (neurips_YYYY.sty).

icml.name: ICML (icml*.sty)
icml.notes: 8 pages at submission (one extra for the camera-ready); references, appendix and the impact statement do not count. Style file name changes every year.

iclr.name: ICLR (iclr*_conference.sty)
iclr.notes: The main-text limit has varied between years (9 or 10 pages): pass --page-limit from the current call for papers.

usenix.name: USENIX Security / OSDI / NSDI (usenix-2020-09.sty)
usenix.notes: USENIX Security bodies are typically limited to 13 pages, systems venues to 12; recent Security cycles also require ethics and open-science sections. Check the call for papers and pass --page-limit.

lncs.name: Springer LNCS (llncs.cls)
lncs.notes: Limits are set per conference and usually include references.

elsevier.name: Elsevier journals (elsarticle), e.g. Computer Networks, Computers & Security
elsevier.body_font: elsarticle preprint 12pt (submission); final typesetting by the publisher
elsevier.notes: Widths are those of the elsarticle 5p two-column layout that authors compile with (\columnwidth 252 pt = 3.49 in, \textwidth 522 pt = 7.22 in), so figures need no scaling in LaTeX; the 1.5-column width (5.51 in) is the publisher's 140 mm artwork size. The publisher's own artwork sizes are 90 / 140 / 190 mm; for a single-column preprint ([preprint,12pt]{elsarticle}) figures are scaled to the text width. Highlights (3-5 bullets of at most 85 characters) usually go in a separate file and keywords in the keyword environment. Declarations, the CRediT statement and the data statement are journal-specific: confirm them and any length limits against the journal's guide for authors.

elsevier-cas.name: Elsevier journals with the CAS template (cas-dc), e.g. Computer Networks
elsevier-cas.body_font: cas-dc 10pt two-column (the journal's own LaTeX template, els-cas-templates)
elsevier-cas.notes: Widths are those of the cas-dc double-column class after \maketitle (\columnwidth 238.25 pt = 3.30 in, \textwidth 494.51 pt = 6.84 in, \columnsep 18 pt), so figures need no scaling in LaTeX; the 1.5-column width (5.51 in) is the publisher's 140 mm artwork size. cas-dc redefines figure and figure* with key-value options: write \begin{figure} (top placement by default) or \begin{figure}[pos=t], never [t] or [!t], which leaves the position empty and sends every figure to the end of the document. The class itself reports a 123.6 pt overfull box at \maketitle (also in the official sample); it is harmless. Numbered references: natbib [numbers] with elsarticle-num, or the template's cas-model2-names for author-year journals. Highlights (3-5 bullets of at most 85 characters) usually go in a separate file. Declarations, the CRediT statement and the data statement are journal-specific: confirm them and any length limits against the journal's guide for authors.
